[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Self-Attention and Multi-Head Attention in Deep Learning"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Attention mechanisms have revolutionized deep learning, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision. By allowing models to weigh the importance of different elements in an input sequence dynamically, attention overcomes the limitations of traditional recurrent neural networks."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Self-Attention"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Self-attention computes a representation of a single sequence by relating different positions of the single sequence to compute a representation of the same sequence. It relies on three primary matrices: Queries (Q), Keys (K), and Values (V)."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Queries (Q): The vector representation of the current token trying to score other tokens."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keys (K): Vectors used to match against queries to determine the attention weights."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Values (V): The actual content vectors that are aggregated based on the calculated attention weights."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"The Scaled Dot-Product Attention Formula"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"The core mathematical operation of self-attention is the scaled dot-product attention, defined as Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax((Q * K^T) / sqrt(d_k)) * V, where d_k represents the dimension of the key vectors."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

def scaled_dot_product_attention(query, key, value, mask=None):
    d_k = query.size(-1)
    scores = torch.matmul(query, key.transpose(-2, -1)) / torch.sqrt(torch.tensor(d_k, dtype=torch.float32))
    if mask is not None:
        scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)
    attention_weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
    output = torch.matmul(attention_weights, value)
    return output, attention_weights"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Extending to Multi-Head Attention"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Multi-head attention extends the single self-attention mechanism by running it multiple times in parallel. Each 'head' projects the queries, keys, and values into different subspaces, allowing the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"import torch.nn as nn

class MultiHeadAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, num_heads):
        super(MultiHeadAttention, self).__init__()
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.head_dim = d_model // num_heads
        
        self.q_linear = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.k_linear = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.v_linear = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.out = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        
    def forward(self, q, k, v, mask=None):
        batch_size = q.size(0)
        
        # Linear projections
        q = self.q_linear(q).view(batch_size, -1, self.num_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        k = self.k_linear(k).view(batch_size, -1, self.num_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        v = self.v_linear(v).view(batch_size, -1, self.num_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        
        scores = torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1)) / torch.sqrt(torch.tensor(self.head_dim, dtype=torch.float32))
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)
        
        attn = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        output = torch.matmul(attn, v)
        
        output = output.transpose(1, 2).contiguous().view(batch_size, -1, self.d_model)
        return self.out(output)"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Self-attention and multi-head attention form the foundational building blocks of modern Transformer architectures. By capturing complex, long-range dependencies efficiently, they continue to drive state-of-the-art performance across diverse machine learning domains."}]
